summary: Default zero-valued ledger timestamps to the database clock, index and sort mixed timestamp formats with fractional precision, and accept both comma-separated local paths and comma-bearing reference values.
reason: Formatting a zero time bypasses the SQL default, datetime() loses fractional ordering and bypasses the timestamp index, while splitting every reference comma corrupts data URLs and splitting none breaks older comma-separated path commands.
validated_outcome: Local tests keep zero-time and historical fractional RFC3339 generations in correct time order, confirm the query uses its expression index, and preserve data URLs, HTTP URLs, comma-bearing filenames, and legacy comma-separated paths.
